sections.heading: Latency Budgets
sections.body: We define budgets for feedback, content display, and task completion. We aim for sub-100ms for acknowledgement, under 1s for above-the-fold content, and clear progressive states beyond that. Budgets guide engineering trade-offs.

sections.heading: Maintaining Flow
sections.body: Flow is fragile. We reduce context switches, preserve focus, and avoid modal interruptions. Whenever possible, we make changes inline. We batch non-urgent updates so the surface doesn’t flicker or jump.

sections.heading: Cognitive Load
sections.body: We measure cognitive load qualitatively: how many decisions before making progress? We trim branches and keep choices mutually exclusive. When advanced options are needed, we group them behind a clear control, not hidden behind mystery meat.

sections.heading: Focus Tools
sections.body: We use spotlighting to guide attention: dim secondary regions during a critical input, increase contrast on the next target, and align motion toward the primary action. Focus tools are temporary and never lock the user in.

sections.heading: Exercises
sections.body: Run a task with a stopwatch and note where time goes. Eliminate one decision and one mode switch. Add an immediate acknowledgement and remeasure.
